thesis.summary: Clear #2 to SpaceX. Real launches/revenue; Neutron is the next leg. ~$54B cap = exception.

catalyst.text: Neutron first launch; national-security launch awards; constellation

thesis.bull: The clear #2 to SpaceX in Western launch, with an operational small-launch vehicle (Electron) generating real revenue and a fast-growing Space Systems business. Neutron, a reusable medium-lift rocket, opens a far larger market and national-security launch demand, giving Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company profile few competitors can match.
thesis.bear: Valuation is rich relative to current revenue and the company is not yet consistently profitable, so the thesis leans heavily on Neutron executing on time — a first-of-its-kind reusable rocket with real technical and schedule risk. A delayed or troubled Neutron debut would compress the multiple sharply. Market cap >$10B makes this a size exception.
invalidationConditions: Neutron's first launch slips materially or fails repeatedly
Electron cadence or Space Systems growth stalls
Capital needs force heavy dilution at depressed prices
unknowns: Path and timeline to sustained profitability is unclear
Neutron development cost-to-completion and first-flight date carry wide error bars
Long-term margin structure of Space Systems vs Launch is unproven

evidence.claim: Electron is an operational orbital launch vehicle with a multi-year flight record
Widely regarded as the leading Western small-launch provider after SpaceX
Neutron targets the larger medium-lift / constellation deployment market
Trades at a high multiple of current revenue (>$10B market cap on ~$0.5B revenue)
